triggers: a kernel on AMD MI308X (CDNA3 / gfx942) risks the '6. Not hoisting loop-invariant global loads wastes 33% performance' trap

payload.goal: Avoid a known trap on AMD MI308X (CDNA3 / gfx942): 6. Not hoisting loop-invariant global loads wastes 33% performance

problem.statement: Pitfalls: FlyDSL Attention Backward dQ + dK+dV on MI308X (gfx942) -- 6. Not hoisting loop-invariant global loads wastes 33% performance

payload.attempted: The inner loop of the dQ kernel iterates over KV-tiles, reloading Q, dO, LSE, and Delta on every iteration. These data are invariant for a fixed Q-tile, but the compiler will not hoist them automatically because they have global memory side effects.
payload.lesson: The FlyDSL/MLIR compiler does not automatically perform loop-invariant code motion (LICM) on global memory accesses. Any loop-invariant global load must be manually hoisted. This is the single largest optimization opportunity in the backward kernel.

established_fact.mechanism: Each iteration re-issues 21 global load instructions (Q: 8, dO: 8, LSE: 1, Delta: 1; mask is variable and not counted). The latency of these loads cannot be hidden by a single wave. After hoisting outside the loop, the values are kept in VGPRs (~40 VGPR), significantly reducing HBM bandwidth pressure.

payload.observed: After manually hoisting outside the loop, dQ improved from 52.43 TFLOPS to 78.23 TFLOPS (+49.2%, latency -33.0%).
